topic: Ship It Right 01/04: Don't ship your app yet

cover.headline: Don’t Ship Your App Yet
cover.subtitle: Important things developers forget before launching their apps.

slides.title: Privacy Policy
slides.tip: Start with a reputable privacy-policy template, then customize it to match your actual product and data practices.
slides.quote: If your app collects personal data, explain what you collect, why you collect it, how you use it, and how users can contact you.

slides.title: Terms & Conditions
slides.tip: Start with a template if useful, but review it for your product. Don’t publish generic terms that describe features you don’t have.
slides.quote: Set clear rules for using your product so users understand their responsibilities and your service’s limits.

slides.title: Remove Frontend Secrets
slides.tip: Keep secrets on the backend, load them through server-side environment variables, and rotate any key that has already been exposed.
slides.quote: Never expose API secrets, private tokens, or credentials in frontend code.

slides.title: Enforce HTTPS
slides.tip: Enable TLS through your hosting provider or CDN, redirect HTTP to HTTPS, and fix mixed-content warnings.
slides.quote: Use HTTPS to protect data in transit between your users and your app.

slides.title: Cookie Consent Banner
slides.tip: Don’t add a banner just for decoration. Configure consent behavior to match the tools you use and the laws that apply.
slides.quote: If your app uses cookies or tracking technologies, check which consent and disclosure rules apply to your users.

slides.title: Ship it or not yet?
slides.description: Be honest. How many are done?

caption.caption:
Don’t ship your app yet. Five things developers forget before launch: a privacy policy, terms, frontend secrets, HTTPS and cookie consent.

General guidance, not legal advice. Check what applies to your users.
